evidence.velocity_vs_rigour: Implement and maintain Data validation processes to improve pipeline accuracy.
evidence.velocity_vs_rigour_explanation: Responsibilities emphasize data validation, governance policy, and accuracy with no velocity/speed language present, placing this at rigour.
evidence.domain_risk: Implement Data governance policy across various projects.
evidence.domain_risk_explanation: Data governance is named but generically across unspecified projects, without financial-reporting or regulatory-audit specifics, placing this at moderate.
evidence.data_team_maturity_explanation: The role leads an existing 'BI-focused sub-squad' and mentors a Junior Analytic Engineer, indicating a growing, structured data team rather than a from-zero build.
evidence.jd_authorship: Develop and optimize Data pipelines using dbt or Dataform, Apache Airflow, Apache Spark, BigQuery, and SQL-based transformations.
evidence.jd_authorship_explanation: Responsibilities name precise tools (dbt/Dataform, Airflow, Spark, BigQuery, LookML, Great Expectations, Apache Iceberg) that show exactly what the role does day to day, written by someone close to the work.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation: Collaborate with BI Developers to ensure dashboards are powered by performant datasets.
evidence.stakeholder_orientation_explanation: The role centers on building the internal data modeling layer that BI developers and dashboards consume, an internal-data orientation.
evidence.autonomy_level: provision, structure, and lead our BI-focused sub-squad... Mentor the Junior Analytic Engineer and provide technical leadership for the sub-squad.
evidence.autonomy_level_explanation: The role combines leadership/mentoring and sub-squad structuring (strategic-leaning) with specific pipeline development and validation tasks (execution), making this mixed.
evidence.ai_role_explanation: No AI tooling or AI-adjacent responsibility is mentioned anywhere in the JD.
evidence.testing_framing: Implement and maintain Data validation processes to improve pipeline accuracy.
evidence.testing_framing_explanation: Data validation is framed as an owned responsibility with explicit ownership verbs (implement, maintain), and named frameworks (Great Expectations, BigQuery Validators) are called out, not just a tool in a skills list.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing: Implement and maintain Data validation processes to improve pipeline accuracy.
evidence.loss_aversion_framing_explanation: Data validation and governance are named as ongoing secondary concerns without regulatory or stakeholder-trust framing dominating the JD, placing this at moderate.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix: Design and implement scalable data models to support BI and analytics.
evidence.greenfield_vs_fix_explanation: The JD mixes new-build language (design and implement data models) with optimize/maintain language (optimize data pipelines, maintain data validation processes) roughly evenly, making this mixed.
evidence.loss_aversion: Implement and maintain Data validation processes to improve pipeline accuracy — a secondary operational-quality concern, not a dominant compliance risk register.
